{{short description|Result in representation theory}}
{{one source |date=May 2024}}
'''Mautner's lemma''' in [[representation theory]], named after Austrian-American mathematician [[Friederich Mautner]], states that if ''G'' is a [[topological group]] and π a [[unitary representation]] of ''G'' on a [[Hilbert space]] ''H'', then for any ''x'' in ''G'', which has [[Glossary of Riemannian and metric geometry#C|conjugate]]s 

:''yxy''<sup>&minus;1</sup>

converging to the [[identity element]] ''e'', for a [[net (mathematics)|net]] of elements ''y'', then any vector ''v'' of ''H'' invariant under all the π(''y'') is also invariant under π(''x'').

==References==
*[[Friederich Ignaz Mautner|F. Mautner]], ''Geodesic flows on symmetric Riemannian spaces'' (1957),  Ann. Math. 65, 416-430
